key_insight: Interfacial lattice distortion in HoFeO3–BaTiO3 nanofibers is consistent with stabilized ferroelectric domains and enhanced hybrid piezoelectric–triboelectric energy harvesting.
engineering_relevance: All-oxide nanofiber heterostructures offer a lead-free route to improving mechanical-energy harvesters embedded in flexible PDMS.
method: Prepare HoFeO3–BaTiO3 heterostructures by alternating sol–gel electrospinning.
Probe crystal structure, interfaces, and polarization using refined XRD, HRTEM, Raman spectroscopy, and electrical measurements.
Encapsulate nanofibers in PDMS and evaluate cyclic-impact output against single-oxide devices.
evidence_signal: The heterostructure delivered 24.31 µW/cm³ at 4.7 MΩ—2.4× the BaTiO3 control—with comparable zero-field polarization and a switching-current peak shifted to a higher field.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify the separate piezoelectric and triboelectric contributions or report long-term cycling durability.
paper_title: Stabilization of Ferroelectric Domains via Interfacial Strain in HoFeO3- BaTiO3 Nanofiber Heterostructures for Enhanced Hybrid Energy Harvesting
